title: Java Iterator
learningObjectives: Obtain an Iterator from a collection.
Use hasNext and next to traverse elements.
Remove the current element safely with Iterator.remove.
Avoid structural modification during enhanced for iteration.
Recognize iterator exhaustion and fail-fast behaviour.

understand.concept: Iterator provides a standard way to traverse a collection one element at a time. hasNext checks whether another element exists, and next returns it while advancing the iterator. Calling next without a remaining element throws NoSuchElementException. Iterator.remove safely removes the last element returned by next when supported. Do not structurally modify a collection directly while iterating over it; use the iterator's removal method or collection operations designed for that purpose.
understand.whyItMatters: This topic helps Java developers select and use the right standard-library tools for java iterator in maintainable applications.
understand.analogy: Think of the collection or date API as a purpose-built tool: its operations communicate the guarantees your program can rely on.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is only a guide; Java API contracts, equality rules and exception behaviour determine the actual result.

explain.narrative: Call iterator() on a collection and loop while hasNext returns true. Each next call advances the cursor. remove is optional and can be called only once after a successful next before another next call. Many standard collection iterators are fail-fast: they may throw ConcurrentModificationException if the collection is structurally changed outside the iterator. This is a bug-detection aid, not a concurrency guarantee.

questions.prompt: Which method checks for another iterator element?
questions.explanation: hasNext indicates whether next can return an element.

questions.prompt: What happens when next is called after exhaustion?
questions.explanation: An exhausted iterator cannot provide another element.

questions.prompt: Which method safely removes the current item during iteration?
questions.explanation: Iterator.remove coordinates removal with the active traversal.

questions.prompt: Why avoid direct structural changes during iteration?
options: They convert the collection to an array
questions.explanation: Fail-fast iterators detect many outside structural modifications.

questions.prompt: How many times may remove be called after one next?
questions.explanation: A successful next call must occur before another iterator remove.
